title: Integrity Commissioner report on Premier Ford and the appointment of the OPP Commissioner
who: Doug Ford (Premier)
subject: Conflict of interest
summary: On requests from opposition MPPs, the Commissioner inquired into whether Premier Ford breached the Members' Integrity Act in the appointment of his friend Ron Taverner as OPP Commissioner. He found no breach of the sections alleged but found the recruitment process flawed.
findings: “Premier Ford did not breach any of the sections of the Act, as alleged.”
“The Premier stayed at arm’s length from the recruitment process and … believed it to be independent.”
The Commissioner found “some troubling aspects of the recruitment process” and concluded the process was flawed.
Recommended an independent, transparent appointment process for the OPP Commissioner.
consequence: No breach found; no penalty. Process recommendation only.

title: Integrity Commissioner report on Minister Bethlenfalvy and a social media ad strategy
who: Peter Bethlenfalvy (President of the Treasury Board)
subject: Other
summary: On a request from MPP Taras Natyshak, the Commissioner examined whether the Minister breached the Act or parliamentary convention through his staff’s social media ad-spend strategy. He found government resources were used for a partisan purpose but did not attribute the breach to the Minister.
findings: “Minister Bethlenfalvy did not breach the MIA or parliamentary convention.”
Government resources, including staff salaried time, “were used for a partisan purpose” in a strategy targeting likely PC supporters, to be funded by the MPP’s riding association.
The Minister “did not appreciate the significance of the ad spend strategy” and “never approved” it.
Made five recommendations on staff training, approval processes and social media guidelines.
consequence: No breach by the Minister; recommendations only.

title: Integrity Commissioner report on Stan Cho and partisan meetings held from a ministry office
who: Stan Cho (MPP; Parliamentary Assistant to the Minister of Finance)
subject: Other
summary: On a request from MPP Stephen Blais, the Commissioner found Mr. Cho breached parliamentary convention by using his Ministry of Finance office to take part in partisan meetings.
findings: “Mr. Cho breached parliamentary convention by using his Ministry of Finance office to participate remotely in partisan meetings.”
He “failed to provide adequate supervision, direction and training to his staff”.
Recommended training of MPP staff on the ethics rules and conventions.
consequence: Breach of parliamentary convention found; no penalty recommended.

title: Integrity Commissioner report on Catherine Fife (NDP) and a budget-feedback email
who: Catherine Fife (MPP, Official Opposition)
subject: Other
summary: On a request from PC MPP Dave Smith, the Commissioner found an opposition MPP breached parliamentary convention when an email from her legislative account linked to a partisan webpage. Included so the record covers all parties.
findings: “It is my opinion that Ms. Fife breached Ontario parliamentary convention with respect to the sending of this email.”
The Commissioner found it “was never her intent” to link to the partisan site, but she did not exercise due diligence.
Recommended no penalty because the breach was inadvertent and promptly addressed.
consequence: Breach found; no penalty recommended.

title: Integrity Commissioner report on Vijay Thanigasalam and a virtual town hall
who: Vijay Thanigasalam (MPP, Scarborough—Rouge Park)
subject: Other
summary: On a request from MPP Taras Natyshak, the Commissioner found the MPP breached parliamentary convention in the organization of an April 9, 2021 virtual town hall that acknowledged the PC candidate for a neighbouring riding.
findings: “It is my opinion that Mr. Thanigasalam breached Ontario parliamentary convention with respect to the organization and conduct of this town hall.”
“It was not his intent to hold a partisan event”; his staff introduced partisan aspects.
He is responsible for his staff’s errors “because he did not adequately train or supervise them”.
consequence: Breach found; no penalty recommended because staff training was arranged.

title: Integrity Commissioner report on Stephen Crawford and long-term care investments
who: Stephen Crawford (MPP; Parliamentary Assistant to the Minister of Infrastructure)
subject: Conflict of interest
summary: On a request from MPP Stephen Blais, the Commissioner examined whether holding investments in long-term care companies created a conflict when Mr. Crawford took part in the Long-Term Care Development Program and Bill 218. He found no breach.
findings: Mr. Crawford had no influence in the decision-making process on the Long-Term Care Development Program.
Bill 218 was “a law of general application”, so a private interest was not engaged; no breach of sections 2 or 4.
Recommended the Legislature consider extending investment restrictions to members and parliamentary assistants.
consequence: No breach found.

title: Integrity Commissioner report on Jessica Bell (NDP) and partisan symbols on constituency materials
who: Jessica Bell (MPP, Official Opposition)
subject: Other
summary: On a request from PC MPP Mike Harris, the Commissioner found an opposition MPP breached parliamentary convention by including NDP logos and riding association references in constituency event materials. Included so the record covers all parties.
findings: “Ms. Bell contravened the Ontario parliamentary convention against using constituency resources for partisan purposes.”
She “promptly admitted her error” and cooperated fully.
Recommended no penalty.
consequence: Breach found; no penalty recommended.

title: Integrity Commissioner report on Randy Hillier (No. 1): constituency resources used for partisan purposes
who: Randy Hillier (MPP, Lanark—Frontenac—Kingston)
subject: Other
summary: On a request from MPP Ian Arthur, the Commissioner found Mr. Hillier breached parliamentary convention in three ways involving constituency office resources and constituent contact information used for partisan messages. He dismissed the allegation of a private-interest conflict.
findings: Breached “the parliamentary convention against using constituency office resources for partisan purposes in three different ways”, including letting his daughter film her federal candidacy announcement in his constituency office.
Directed staff to perform partisan activities without an accountability framework.
Collected constituent contact information into two databases and used it to send partisan messages.
consequence: Reprimand recommended to the Legislative Assembly.

title: Integrity Commissioner report on Randy Hillier (No. 2): social media posts naming individuals
who: Randy Hillier (MPP, Lanark—Frontenac—Kingston)
subject: Other
summary: On a request from MPP Peggy Sattler, the Commissioner found social media posts naming and showing individuals who had become seriously ill or died, with an unfounded claim that COVID-19 vaccines were involved, breached parliamentary convention.
findings: The posts “amounted to a breach of parliamentary convention that might readily be presumed”.
The Commissioner weighed the Assembly’s swift censure, Mr. Hillier’s public apology and his admission of mistakes.
consequence: Reprimand recommended to the Legislative Assembly.

title: Integrity Commissioner report on Minister Clark and the 2022 Greenbelt removals
who: Steve Clark (Minister of Municipal Affairs and Housing)
Ryan Amato (Chief of Staff to Minister Clark)
subject: Greenbelt
summary: On a request from MPP Marit Stiles, the Commissioner inquired into the decision to remove or redesignate lands in the Greenbelt. He concluded Minister Clark breached sections 2 and 3(2) of the Members’ Integrity Act, largely through his chief of staff’s conduct, which he attributed to the Minister.
findings: “Minister Clark breached sections 2 and 3(2) of the Act.”
Mr. Amato “was the driving force behind a flawed process which provided an advantage to those who approached him.”
Of 15 properties removed or redesignated, Mr. Amato “was involved in the selection of 14”.
Mr. Amato’s communications to developers “must be attributed to Mr. Clark” because he failed to oversee an important initiative in his ministry.
The Commissioner believed the Minister was unaware of that process.
consequence: Reprimand recommended to the Legislative Assembly. Mr. Clark apologized. Whether the Assembly adopted the reprimand was not confirmed.

response.text: “I regret that I didn’t provide the sufficient oversight,” and “the buck stops with me.” Mr. Clark did not resign.

title: Auditor General special report on changes to the Greenbelt
who: Ministry of Municipal Affairs and Housing
Ryan Amato (Chief of Staff to the Housing Minister)
subject: Greenbelt
summary: The Auditor General examined the 2022 removal of 15 sites from the Greenbelt. She concluded site selection was not transparent, fair, objective or fully informed.
findings: “How the land sites were selected was not transparent, fair, objective, or fully informed.”
There was sufficient land for the 1.5 million homes target “without the need to build on the Greenbelt”.
“Direct access to the Housing Minister’s Chief of Staff resulted in certain prominent developers receiving preferential treatment.”
About 92% of the roughly 7,400 acres removed came from five sites put forward by two developers.
Owners could see more than $8.3 billion in added land value.
consequence: The government restored the lands (Bill 136, December 2023). A 2025 follow-up found 95% of the Auditor General’s recommended actions fully implemented.
timeline: Bill 136 royal assent, restoring the lands

title: Integrity Commissioner: no inquiry into Premier Ford and two family wedding events
who: Doug Ford (Premier)
subject: Fundraising
summary: On a February 2023 request from MPP Marit Stiles about a stag and doe and a wedding for the Premier’s daughter, the Commissioner found insufficient grounds to hold an inquiry into breaches of sections 2, 4 or 6(1).
findings: “There are insufficient grounds … to warrant an inquiry as to whether Premier Ford breached sections 2, 4 or sub-section 6(1) of the Act.”
The Act “does not concern itself with appearances of a conflict, only actual conflicts” (interim report).
Only one developer with Greenbelt removals attended the wedding.
consequence: No inquiry; no finding of breach.

title: RCMP criminal investigation related to the Greenbelt
who: Government of Ontario figures (not publicly named by the RCMP)
subject: Greenbelt
summary: The RCMP opened a criminal investigation after the Auditor General and Integrity Commissioner reports. The last public update, in October 2025, said it was ongoing; reports in October 2026 say there are no updates.
findings: The RCMP has said the investigation is ongoing and has withheld details to protect it.
No charges have been announced.
consequence: No charges or conclusion reported as of November 2026.

title: Integrity Commissioner closes an inquiry into Kaleed Rasheed without a finding
who: Kaleed Rasheed (former Minister of Public and Business Service Delivery)
subject: Greenbelt
summary: An inquiry requested by MPP Marit Stiles in October 2023 concerned a 2020 Las Vegas trip with a Greenbelt-linked developer. The office closed it without a finding because inquiries must be suspended when an election is called and the requester did not ask to restart it.
findings: Under the Act, an inquiry is suspended when an election is called and resumes only if the requester asks within 30 days afterwards. That did not happen.
No finding on Mr. Rasheed was made.
consequence: Inquiry closed with no finding. Mr. Rasheed left cabinet in November 2023.

response.text: Mr. Rasheed called a mistake in dates he gave the Commissioner “an honest mistake”.

timeline: Commissioner says he will not investigate the trip “at this time” (CTV)

title: Auditor General audit of the Ontario Place redevelopment
who: Ministry of Infrastructure
Infrastructure Ontario
subject: Procurement
summary: The Auditor General audited the call for development for Ontario Place. She found the process was not fair, transparent or accountable to all participants and that many rules were not followed.
findings: The process was “not fair, transparent, or accountable to all participants”; criteria were finalized after the deadline.
Three bidders met with the ministry and the Premier’s Office during the open period, “contrary to CFD Rules”.
An Infrastructure Ontario vice-president communicated directly with Therme during the communications ban; no minutes of bidder meetings were kept.
Estimated public cost rose by $1.8 billion since 2019, to $2.2 billion.
consequence: The Public Accounts Committee held hearings in November 2025 and reported in October 2026. No minister was found in breach.

response.text: Deputy Premier Sylvia Jones, answering for the minister, said she saw no reason the minister should step down (paraphrased by Global News).

title: Auditor General finding that the zoning order process needs an overhaul
who: Ministry of Municipal Affairs and Housing
subject: MZOs
summary: The Auditor General’s 2024 annual report found the minister’s zoning order process needed to be overhauled. According to the Canadian Press, Ontario used zoning orders 114 times from 2019 to 2023, 17 times as often as in the previous two decades.
findings: “No protocol or rationale for prioritizing some zoning order requests over others.”
The ministry did not give the minister complete and timely information about incoming requests.
Recommended recording the reasoning for each order.

title: Integrity Commissioner: no inquiry into Minister Surma and the Ontario Place project
who: Kinga Surma (Minister of Infrastructure)
subject: Procurement
summary: On an October 2024 request from MPP Marit Stiles, the Commissioner found insufficient grounds to inquire into whether Minister Surma breached sections 2 and 3 over Ontario Place and the Therme agreement. He did not examine whether the process itself was flawed.
findings: “There are insufficient grounds for me to conduct an inquiry into whether Minister Surma breached either section 2 or section 3 of the Act.”
The Act does not cover “apparent” conflicts of interest.
The Minister’s counsel disputed the alleged irregularities.
consequence: No inquiry; no finding.

title: Lobbyist Registrar publishes non-compliance by consultant lobbyist Nico Fidani-Diker
who: Nico Fidani-Diker (consultant lobbyist)
subject: Lobbying
summary: The Registrar found a consultant lobbyist did not comply with the Lobbyists Registration Act on several matters, including Greenbelt removals and zoning-order filings, and published his name rather than imposing a ban.
findings: Failed to register after lobbying a public office holder on a client’s Greenbelt removal request in 2022.
Offered two public office holders hockey tickets, placing them “in a position of real or potential conflict of interest”.
Contravened the conflict prohibition in lobbying two public office holders with whom he had close working, political and personal relationships.
Failed to give particulars of the regulation change sought in two filings (a Greenbelt regulation and a zoning order).
consequence: Name and summary published; no lobbying ban.

response.text: “These oversights were mine and mine alone.” He accepted “full responsibility”.

title: Lobbyist Registrar bans John Mutton from lobbying for two years
who: John Mutton (consultant lobbyist; former mayor of Clarington)
subject: Lobbying
summary: The Registrar found repeated non-compliance with the Lobbyists Registration Act between 2016 and 2023, including unregistered lobbying on zoning orders and the Greenbelt, contingency fees, gifts and a political fundraiser. The Registrar’s public summary does not name the public office holders involved.
findings: Failed to register after lobbying two public office holders on a client’s zoning-order request; paid a $300,000 contingency fee.
Lobbied on a Greenbelt removal; offered a round of golf and Raptors tickets; paid a $225,000 contingency fee.
Lobbied on a second client’s zoning order for a $100,000 contingency fee, and in 2023 on a third client’s for a $250,000 contingency fee not yet payable.
“Organized a political fundraiser raising more than $25,000 for the public office holder’s riding association approximately two months prior to the beginning of the 2022 provincial election.”
Conduct “undermine[s] the Act’s purpose of transparency and public confidence in the independence of public sector decision making.”
consequence: Prohibited from lobbying Ontario public office holders from April 17, 2025 to April 17, 2027; name and summary published.

title: Registrar’s report on lobbyist John Mutton is reported to quote texts with PC MPP Laurie Scott about zoning orders and fundraising
who: Laurie Scott (PC MPP, Haliburton—Kawartha Lakes—Brock)
John Mutton (consultant lobbyist)
subject: MZOs
summary: A 132-page Lobbyist Registrar report on Mr. Mutton, dated January 29, 2025 and supplied to The Trillium by Mr. Mutton, quotes text messages between Ms. Scott and Mr. Mutton from December 2021 to July 2023. The report concerns Mr. Mutton’s compliance with the Lobbyists Registration Act. It made no formal ruling on Ms. Scott’s conduct. This entry relies on The Highlander’s reporting because The Trillium’s article could not be opened.
findings: As reported by The Highlander: the Commissioner found Mr. Mutton breached the Act about a dozen times and put Ms. Scott “in a position of potential conflict of interest”.

The report found Ms. Scott and Mr. Mutton “clearly communicated in an effort to move forward” a provincial zoning-order decision. The orders concerned Kawartha Downs and Brown’s Line in Cavan Monaghan.
The Commissioner did not determine whether Ms. Scott meaningfully helped either order be approved, and made no formal ruling on her conduct.
A text of February 2, 2023, as quoted: “do you think you could get a couple of your people … They have to go thru my portal so I get credit.”
consequence: No finding against Ms. Scott. As of November 6, 2026 no inquiry into her has been confirmed open. The Highlander reports NDP Leader Marit Stiles asked the Integrity Commissioner to investigate.

response.text: Her office received a zoning-order request endorsed by the municipality, and the order followed the ministry’s established process. “All information on donations and donors is publicly available.” (as reported; full statement not seen)
response.by: Laurie Scott, statement to The Trillium and The Highlander

timeline: Earliest text quoted in the report
Text asking Mr. Mutton for “a couple of your people”
Latest text quoted in the report
Registrar publishes Mr. Mutton’s two-year lobbying ban
The Highlander reports on the texts

title: Integrity Commissioner: no inquiry into Premier Ford and three ministers over the Dresden landfill
who: Doug Ford (Premier)
Andrea Khanjin (former Minister of the Environment)
Todd McCarthy (Minister of the Environment)
Stephen Lecce (Minister of Energy and Mines)
subject: Conflict of interest
summary: On a May 2025 request from MPP Ted Hsu based on two Trillium stories, the Commissioner found no reasonable and probable grounds to inquire into whether the four breached the Act in including the Dresden landfill in Bill 5. He made no findings on the underlying facts.
findings: “Mr. Hsu has not put forward sufficient evidence to establish reasonable and probable grounds.”
“No evidence of any relationship between the members and the owners of the Dresden Landfill.”
“I have made no findings about the underlying facts of this matter.”
consequence: No inquiry; no finding.

response.text: All four denied contravening the Act and cited reducing reliance on U.S. landfills (as summarized by the Commissioner).

title: Auditor General finding on the Skills Development Fund Training Stream
who: Office of the Minister of Labour, Immigration, Training and Skills Development
subject: Procurement
summary: The Auditor General found the application selection process was not fair, transparent or accountable. More than half of the applications approved by the minister’s office had been rated lower against the program’s criteria.
findings: “549 applications, more than half (54%) of the applications approved for funding by the Minister’s Office, were rated Poor, Low, or Medium.”
These received “$742 million, or 56% of total funding across the first five rounds”.
“670 applications that ranked High … were not selected for funding, with little rationale.”
“The selection process was not fair, transparent or accountable.”
consequence: The ministry agreed with all four recommendations. See the related Integrity Commissioner inquiry.

response.text: The ministry agreed with all four of the audit’s recommendations.
response.by: Office of the Auditor General (news release)

title: Integrity Commissioner inquiry into Minister Piccini and the Skills Development Fund
who: David Piccini (Minister of Labour, Immigration, Training and Skills Development)
subject: Procurement
summary: On requests from the NDP and the Liberals, the Commissioner opened an inquiry under the Members’ Integrity Act into how applicants were selected in the fourth and fifth rounds of the Skills Development Fund Training Stream. No report had been found as of November 6, 2026.
findings: The inquiry’s scope is whether Mr. Piccini contravened the Act or parliamentary convention in selecting applicants.
No conclusions had been reached as of the December 2025 reports; later status could not be confirmed.
consequence: None yet.

response.text: “I know he’ll co-operate with the integrity commissioner.”

timeline: Auditor General’s report on the fund

title: Divisional Court: failure to consult on zoning-order changes in Bill 197 was unreasonable and unlawful
who: Steve Clark (Minister of Municipal Affairs and Housing)
subject: MZOs
summary: In a challenge by Greenpeace and the Wilderness Committee, the Divisional Court held the Minister acted “unreasonably and unlawfully” by not consulting the public on changes to zoning-order rules in Bill 197. Other challenged changes were found permissible.
findings: The Minister acted “unreasonably and unlawfully” by failing to consult on the amendments under the Environmental Bill of Rights.
Posting the changes after they became law did not meet the Environmental Bill of Rights.
consequence: Declaration only; the legislation remains in force.
timeline: Decision (some outlets give a slightly later date)
